regime.skew: flat at 25D (-0.1), put-rich in the tail (950 put IV 15.9 vs 1050 call IV 12.8)
regime.label: Dealer short-gamma below the 1030 flip, with fresh downside insurance feeding the accelerant
evidence: -6,097 net GEX within +/-20 points of the 1004.9 anchor: dealers are short gamma around spot, so they sell futures into weakness and amplify the move rather than fade it.

1030 is the per-strike GEX sign flip (-714 at 1020, +526 at 1030) and spot sits 25.1 points below it; cumulative net GEX never crosses zero across the 950-1150 chain, ending at -9,985, so the whole live strike range is dealer-short-gamma.
+770 put OI added today, 100% of it below spot (+517 at 950, +187 at 970, +81 each at 990 and 1000) while call OI fell 124 at 1050 and 116 at 1070 - insurance accumulating, upside calls being closed.
960 put wall holds 3,213 OI and traded 438 contracts with put IV at 14.9 vs 13.1 ATM - Vol2Vol confirms this wall is live, not stale structural OI.

S50Z26.today_summary: 1004.9 future closed down 3 points, extending a 20.3-point two-session slide from 1025.2 and leaving spot 25.1 points below the static 1030 max pain. Put/call volume ratio jumped to 1.63 from 0.63 yesterday on 2,657 put contracts, and all 770 contracts of new put OI landed below spot. Net GEX around the anchor is -6,097, so dealers hedge with the move; the live downside structure is the 1000 strike (2,393 put OI, 404 lots traded) and then the 960 wall (3,213 put OI). ATM IV at 13.12% is up 1.78 points from the 11.34% low on 14 Nov, a fourth straight session of expansion.
what_changed: Dealer gamma flipped sign: ATM net GEX went from +90 on 17 Nov to -5,896 on 18 Nov and -6,097 today, turning dealers from stabilisers into amplifiers in a single session.
Near-money put wall migrated 1000 -> 960 on 18 Nov, following spot down; the overall put wall and the active near-money wall now coincide at 960, unlike a stale deep wall.
Put/call volume ratio went 1.11 -> 0.63 -> 1.63 across the last three sessions, the highest flow-side put bias of the series' life.
ATM IV expanded four straight sessions, 11.34% -> 11.80% -> 12.48% -> 13.12%, lifting the 1-sigma daily move from 7.33 to 8.31 points.
S50Z26.five_day_thesis: Five sessions ago on 12 Nov the future was 1019.0 with ATM net GEX at -3,597 and cumulative GEX at -3,138; today spot is 14.1 points lower at 1004.9 and cumulative GEX is 3.2x more negative at -9,985. The decisive event was 18 Nov, when ATM GEX flipped from +90 to -5,896 - the series spent 14 and 17 Nov in mild dealer long gamma and has now moved decisively short, which is the highest-signal change in the window. Put OI grew 2,332 contracts (+15.1%) from 15,480 to 17,812 while call OI added only 1,884 and is now shrinking above 1050, so the burden map has tilted downside while IV expanded rather than compressed - the real-flow signature, not stale OI. Max pain has not moved off 1030 for seven straight sessions while spot walked 21.3 points away from it since 14 Nov, so the gap is being created by flow beating the structure, not by the structure pulling price. With 40 days left and the anchor below the flip, the 1030 magnet should be treated as a ceiling reference rather than a target to fade toward.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 1000 / 960
strategies.rationale: The matrix maps short gamma plus a downside Squeeze plus expanding IV to a defined-risk put debit spread sited at the live structure: long the 1000 strike where 2,393 put OI and 404 lots make it today's active battleground, short the 960 wall where 3,213 put OI is the point the forced flow should stall.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = the net debit, 10.8 points at the offer (15.9 paid for the 1000 put less 5.1 received for the 960 put), about 10.1 points at mids. Max gain = 40-point width less debit = 29.2 points; breakeven 989.2.
strategies.invalidation: A sustained reclaim of 1030 - the GEX sign flip - puts dealers back in long gamma above spot and voids the amplification premise.

strategies.name: Put debit spread 980 / 950
strategies.rationale: Cheaper tail insurance that also harvests 2.77 vol points of wing skew: it buys the 25-delta 980 put at 13.13% IV and sells the 10-delta 950 put at 15.90%, the richest put IV in the chain and the strike that absorbed 585 lots and +517 OI today.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = the net debit, 4.7 points at the offer (8.9 paid for the 980 put less 4.2 received for the 950 put), about 4.5 points at mids. Max gain = 30-point width less debit = 25.3 points; breakeven 975.3.
strategies.invalidation: A move back above 1020 with put OI at 950 ceasing to build removes the insurance-demand driver behind the structure.

strategies.name: Call credit spread 1030 / 1050
strategies.rationale: Net GEX is positive at every strike from 1030 up (+526 at 1030, +928 at 1040, +1,022 at 1050), so dealers are long gamma above the flip and fade rallies there, while 1,783 call OI at 1050 and today's call OI drawdown of 124 at 1050 and 116 at 1070 show the upside being unwound rather than built.
strategies.defined_risk: Max loss = 20-point width less the 4.1-point credit (7.1 received for the 1030 call less 3.0 paid for the 1050 call) = 15.9 points. The short strike carries a 0.239 delta, so roughly a 1-in-4 risk-neutral chance of finishing in the money; short-vol payoff is negative-skew and the capped loss is real, so this is the smallest-conviction leg of the three.
strategies.invalidation: A sustained close above 1030 with call volume building puts the short strike in the money and breaks the long-gamma-fades-rallies premise.

S50Z26.prediction: Bias stays lower while 1004.9 holds below the 1030 flip: with dealers short 6,097 of gamma around the anchor and an 8.31-point 1-sigma day, a break of the 1000 strike should see dealer hedging add to the move toward the 960 wall rather than cushion it. The bearish case is invalidated by a sustained reclaim of 1030, which restores dealer long gamma and converts the regime to pinning around max pain. Do not fade toward the 1030 max pain simply because spot is 25.1 points below it - IV expanding 1.78 points and put volume at 1.63x calls are the max-pain-failure signature of real flow outrunning the option structure.
S50Z26.risk_note: Educational analysis only - not trade advice, and no recommendation to execute anything. SET50 options are European and cash-settled on the SET50 index with no physical delivery, so the dealer-hedging mechanics behind pinning are structurally weaker here than for share-settled single stocks: treat the 1030 max pain and the 960 wall as tendencies, not guarantees. Open interest is a burden map, not a directional vote - it never reveals who is long or short, hedge or speculation, and heavy put OI below spot is frequently insurance rather than a bearish bet. Defined risk is not risk-free: every max loss quoted above does happen, and macro or news flow can override the option structure outright.
